speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you been experiencing the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, joint pain, and skin lesions, could you describe exactly what the skin lesions look like and where they are located?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Early Lyme disease (Erythema Migrans) or early disseminated Syphilis. The combination of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands, history of camping in Minnesota, and recent self-resolving knee pain strongly suggests Lyme disease, though syphilis remains a differential. I will proceed with serological testing to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology (ELISA and Western Blot). REQUEST TEST: RPR_and_VDRL. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_diff.
